items.evidence: REPRODUCES (flipped from 26.1.2's pass: 1.21.10's vanilla uses camelCase gamerules). Vanilla 1.21.10's integrated tree has 59 gamerule literals, all camelCase (doFireTick, keepInventory, commandModificationBlockLimit, maxCommandForkCount, locatorBar, ...); the jar's GameRules clinit registers 60 keys, the 60th (minecartMaxSpeed) feature-gated out of the tree. The Rust /gamerule tree is built from available_rules() snake_case engine names plus minecraft:-prefixed forms (vanilla.rs:315-326), so every vanilla name is unusable in the port. Count differs by one more: vanilla's fire pair (doFireTick + allowFireTicksAwayFromPlayer) collapses into the single engine rule fire_spread_radius_around_player (gamerules.rs:66-72, default 128), so the engine table has 58 entries against vanilla's 59 keys (plus gated MAX_MINECART_SPEED, gamerules.rs:130). The port HAS the full camelCase mapping (vanilla_key / from_vanilla_key, gamerules.rs:151-230, all 26 renames + the vanilla_inverted trio) and fire-pair handling (fire_radius / fire_keys, gamerules.rs:236-260) but only for level.dat persistence, not the command tree. Sampled defaults match vanilla exactly (randomTickSpeed 3, maxEntityCramming 24, maxCommandChainLength 65536, maxCommandForkCount 65536, tntExplosionDropDecay false, keepInventory false, snowAccumulationHeight 1). Corpus carries 255 gamerule cases (report §2).
items.title: /gamerule exposes the 26.3 snake_case table; vanilla 1.21.10 uses camelCase names

items.evidence: REPRODUCES — four extras (26.1.2 had three; swing joins because vanilla 1.21.10 has no /swing at all). Rust release tree 78 literals vs vanilla 1.21.10's integrated tree 74 (oracle export): 74 of 74 present, zero missing; extras compute, posteffect, swing, unpublish. posteffect: no PostEffectCommand class in the 1.21.10 jar, no posteffect in datagen commands.json or the oracle tree, no minecraft:post_effects registry in 1.21.10's registries.json, so ArgType::Id("post_effects") (tree_extra.rs:40,50) references a nonexistent registry; registered unconditionally (tree_extra.rs:36-53). unpublish: no UnpublishCommand class in the jar (arrived in 26.2); registered unconditionally (tree_extra.rs:83-85). compute: no ComputeCommand class in the jar; registered unconditionally (tree_data.rs:51-69); the /data modify ... compute source is also present (shared context_sources helper, tree_data.rs:32-48), counted here per the 26.1.2 precedent. swing: no SwingCommand class in the jar, no swing in the dump or tree, no swing_animation argument type in vanilla's 57-entry table; registered unconditionally with animation + duration args (tree_world.rs:176-192). Corpus carries edge cases for all four (report §2).
items.method: tree diff vs oracle tree.json + datagen commands.json + driver run
items.title: Four 26.x commands in the release tree; vanilla 1.21.10 has none of them

items.evidence: REPRODUCES (both parts). Vanilla 1.21.10 still has the OLD selector parser — the option-state refactor (InvertableSetOptionState, SetOnceOptionState) that closed this defect for 26.2 had NOT happened yet in 1.21.10 (neither class exists in the 1.21.10 server-game jar). (a) Duplicate options: vanilla 1.21.10's EntitySelectorOptions.get() runs the canUse gate BEFORE the value is read — parseOptions calls get() at offset 65, right after readString, before the = and value (Selector.javap:651-720) — but does NOT roll back: only the unknown-option branch does setCursor(start) (offsets 47-52); the inapplicable branch throws ERROR_INAPPLICABLE_OPTION at the cursor as it stands, i.e. at the END of the option name. Rust rolls back to the option-name START (selector.rs:331-341, rollback(reader, start, ...)). Three-version shape: 1.21.7 vanilla at the end of the VALUE, 1.21.10/26.1-line vanilla at the end of the NAME, 26.2 vanilla at the START — Rust reports at the start in all cases, matching only 26.2. (b) @a[type=player]: vanilla 1.21.10's type option canUse is !parser.isTypeLimited() (lambda$bootStrap$47, SelectorOptions2.javap:862-872), and @a/@p/@r all call limitToType(EntityType.PLAYER) during parseSelector (offsets 165, 196, 225) — so vanilla REJECTS @a[type=player]. Rust pushes minecraft:player into s.types for @a/@p/@r (selector.rs:218-242) without marking type_option, so can_use("type") stays true and Rust ACCEPTS it.
items.title: Selector option errors: wrong cursor on duplicates; type= accepted for @a/@p/@r

items.title: /worldborder set/add time (1.21.7: Time argument vs integer) — fixed: tree uses integer(0)

items.evidence: CLOSED against real vanilla. The 1.21.7 item claimed vanilla suggests no recipes for /recipe and Rust suggests the learnable set. items.evidence: REPRODUCES as a prepared-data gap — the 1.21.7 condition (26.1.2's was closed). The prepared copy used for the run (versions/1.21.10/.local/horizon-client/1.21.10/, from candidate-test) had command-registries.json, commands.json and registries.json but NO assets/ directory at all — no lang file. Mitigated for the run by extracting assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json from the 1.21.10 client jar (md5 d166df536bf7f617599990f8437ba18c, jar-identical, 7,583 keys, contains argument.entity.invalid; deprecated.json also extracted) — exactly what the port's own horizon-prepare languages step does. The prepare flow itself produces the file, so the fix is a re-prepare, not code. Error-text count in report §2.6 confirms the mitigation worked.
items.method: md5 vs client jar + fixture source + driver run

systemic_note: The 1.21.10 command surface carries 26.3-era tree code against a 1.21.10 vanilla that predates it: four extra top-level commands (compute, posteffect, swing, unpublish), the 26.3 snake_case gamerule table against vanilla's camelCase rules (G01 flips from 26.1.2's pass to a gap), the 26.3 62-entry argument-type table against vanilla's 57 (G13), SlotSource in place of item_slot/item_slots (G12), and 1.21.7-era parse code (particle/modifier handling, selector rollback) that the 26.2 port fixed but this tree never carried. The era template DID adapt some command code (/worldborder integer time — G10 fixed in-tree, clock-free /time, no stopwatch, fetchprofile name+id, the gamerule persistence mapping) but the adaptations stop at the tree's edge: the release tree, the argument-type table, and the oracles were carried verbatim from 26.3. All three in-scope oracles fail with the 1.21.7 forms (O01 6 errors, O02 19 client errors, O03 18 errors), and the linchpin VanillaCommandExecOracle fails with 45 errors (B9-O05, NEW — it passed in 26.1.2). 13 of 17 primary 1.21.7 items reproduce; G04 is closed by a vanilla change (Angle->Rotation), G10 fixed in-tree, G11 closed against real vanilla; G19 is withdrawn (vanilla 1.21.10 has no /swing at all). H01 stays fixed: the probe compiles, so the command_parse measurement ran end-to-end. The remaining risk is execution, not parsing: 17 of 22 drivers are unrun e2e drivers, and command_exec is now oracle-blocked too.
